text:
ana: Heads up — I'm seeing a weird gap between the decision logs and the full evals for the routing policy that handles header overrides.

ana: Several /v1/generate requests with header `X-Route-Force: dedicated` did not emit a decision-log entry even though we have a 1% sampling rate for that policy.

josh: Did you grep logs by request-id or trace-id? Sampling keys changed last week.

ana: I started with trace-id first: `trace=01f3a8c2` and then looked for `policy=pid-47` in decision-logs. Nothing. Full runtime shows the route matched and we returned the dedicated model.

priya: Can you paste the eval trace and the decision engine debug line? Might be a hashing mismatch.

ana: Paste of the runtime line from the serving node: `matched route /v1/generate -> policy pid-47 (header override)`, then `applied variant=dedicated-v2`. Also saw `eval_path=runtime::match_headers` in the span.

sam: Here's the snippet I pulled from decision-logger for the same time window (no entries for pid-47):
```
# decision-logger tail
time=2026-01-12T09:12:43Z module=decision-logger level=info policy=pid-12 decisions=124
time=2026-01-12T09:12:44Z module=decision-logger level=info policy=pid-55 decisions=3
```

priya: Hmm. Two quick hypotheses: 1) sampling key used by decision-logger is different (we switched to `request_id % 100` hashing but runtime uses `sha256(header_value) % 100`), 2) logs are being sharded to a different collector due to routing by region.

josh: Agree. I remember a deploy that changed the sampling key last month to `hash(span.trace_id)` for uniformity. If runtime still uses header hash, mismatch will happen.

ana: I checked the config in console -> policies -> pid-47 -> advanced: shows `sampling: 0.01` and `sampling_key: request_id`. But runtime source code in the candidate PR uses `header_value` for header overrides (code comment: // sampling by override header).

sam: So decision-logger will only see samples when the request_id % 100 < 1, but runtime might be selecting based on header hash -> inconsistent sets.

infra-bot: @ana @sam Sampling for policy pid-47 increased to 100% for 60s by infra-bot (manual debug window).

ana: Thanks — I enabled that while we triage. After enabling, decision-logger shows entries for pid-47 matching the traces. Seems like the logger is fine when sampling is aligned.

priya: Can you dump the policy config we push to the agent? There are two places: control-plane policy JSON and agent local override. If they differ, that would explain it.

ana: Agent config (on node a3-12):
```
{
  "policy_id": "pid-47",
  "sampling_rate": 0.01,
  "sampling_key": "request_id",
  "match": {"path_prefix": "/v1/generate", "header": "X-Route-Force"}
}
```

ana: Control-plane shows `sampling_key: header_value` in the policy history (PR #842). So control-plane and agent disagree.

josh: That's the bug then — the rollout UI applied the new sampling_key but the agent-side rollout failed to pick up the change for some hosts because of a stale cache TTL in the config agent. We changed TTL to 10m recently.

sam: Which hosts are affected? I can force a config reload for the cluster that serves EU-east.

ana: Looks like only a3-12 and a3-13 (both eu-east) still had the old policy. Other hosts picked up header_value.

sre-oncall: We're noticing spike in decision-log volume when infra-bot set to 100% — expected. Reverting after triage?

priya: Two recommended actions: 1) fix the config-agent TTL bug (PR incoming), 2) add a transient override in the decision-logger to accept `trace_id` sampling key mapping so we can correlate until rollout completes. Also add a tiny UI hint in console next to sampling_key to warn if agent/plane configs differ.

josh: I'll raise the PR for config-agent TTL fix and add a health check that alerts when policy hashes diverge between control-plane and agents.

ana: For immediate debugging we added `X-Force-Decision-Log: true` header to a handful of requests and verified decision logs. That gave us enough evidence.

sam: For postmortem: we should also sample by composite key (request_id + header_value) for 24h for pid-47 so we get cross-coverage while the fix rolls out.

infra-bot: Scheduled composite sampling window: pid-47 composite_key sampling at 0.05 for 24h starting 2026-01-12T09:20:00Z.

ana: One UX ask: add a single-click "force_trace" header toggle in the route debug panel so engineers can repro without hitting infra-bot. Right now it's two manual steps.

priya: Agreed. Also we should surface a small diff on the policy page showing "last applied to agents" vs "control-plane" with a link to agent list.

josh: I'll prototype the diff link. Priya, can you own the decision-logger fallback for transient key mapping?

priya: Yup. I'll also add test vectors to the regression suite to catch sampling_key drift.

ana: Thanks all — after the agent reload and the temporary sampling window the discrepancy is resolved. Leaving the debug window open another 30m then revert.

sre-oncall: Noting for oncall timeline: 09:12 detected, 09:15 infra-bot 100% window, 09:20 composite sampling, 09:30 patch PR opened, 09:40 agent reload, 09:45 discrepancy cleared.

ana: Closing thread once PR merges. :thumbsup:
